books.name: Key Word Castle
books.focus: wish · might · can't have · if · needn't have

items.a: I regret not studying for the test.
items.tip: Regrets about the past: wish + past perfect: I wish I had studied.
items.say: I wish I had studied for the test.

items.a: It's possible that the dragon is sleeping.
items.tip: It's possible that … = might + verb: The dragon might be sleeping.
items.say: The dragon might be sleeping.

items.a: I'm sure Ella didn't break the vase.
items.tip: Sure something didn't happen = can't have + past participle.
items.say: Ella can't have broken the vase.

items.a: We didn't win because we didn't train.
items.tip: Third conditional: would have won if we had trained (past perfect after if).
items.say: We would have won if we had trained.

items.a: It wasn't necessary for us to bring food, but we did.
items.tip: needn't have + past participle = we did it, but it wasn't necessary.
items.say: We needn't have brought food.

items.a: Please don't make so much noise.
items.tip: I'd rather + someone + past simple = I want them to (not) do it.
items.say: I'd rather you didn't make so much noise.

items.a: It's a long time since I went ice-skating.
items.tip: It's a long time since… = I haven't … for ages.
items.say: I haven't been ice-skating for ages.

items.a: My dad said I could stay up late.
items.tip: let + person + base verb (no to): let me stay.
items.say: My dad let me stay up late.

books.name: Owl's Tricky Turns
books.focus: is said to · had my hair cut · called off · reminded me to

items.a: People say that the forest is haunted.
items.tip: People say that X is… = X is said to be…
items.say: The forest is said to be haunted.

items.a: They are going to repair the bridge next week.
items.tip: Future passive: is going to be / will be + past participle.
items.say: The bridge is going to be repaired next week.

items.a: 'I'll help you with your homework,' said Zoe.
items.tip: offer + to + verb: Zoe offered to help me.
items.say: Zoe offered to help me with my homework.

items.a: I'm really looking forward to the school trip.
items.tip: can't wait for = be very excited about something in the future.
items.say: I can't wait for the school trip.

items.a: A hairdresser cut my hair yesterday.
items.tip: have something done = someone else does it for you: I had my hair cut.
items.say: I had my hair cut yesterday.

items.a: Mo cancelled the party because it rained.
items.tip: call off = cancel.
items.say: Mo called off the party because it rained.

items.a: I started this puzzle two hours ago.
items.b: I ___ this puzzle for two hours.
items.tip: Started in the past and still going: have been + -ing + for.
items.say: I have been doing this puzzle for two hours.

items.a: 'Don't forget your swimsuit,' Mum said to me.
items.tip: remind + person + to + verb: Mum reminded me to bring my swimsuit.
items.say: Mum reminded me to bring my swimsuit.

books.name: Spell Words
books.focus: so … that · despite · no point · used to + -ing

items.a: Ravi was too tired to finish the race.
items.b: Ravi was ___ he couldn't finish the race.
items.tip: too tired to… = so tired that … couldn't…
items.say: Ravi was so tired that he couldn't finish the race.

items.a: Although it was raining, we played outside.
items.tip: despite + noun or -ing (not despite + a full clause): despite the rain.
items.say: Despite the rain, we played outside.

items.a: It's not worth watching that film.
items.tip: It's not worth …ing = There's no point (in) …ing.
items.say: There's no point in watching that film.

items.a: Jack doesn't usually get up early.
items.tip: be used to + -ing = be familiar with something: Jack isn't used to getting up early.
items.say: Jack isn't used to getting up early.

items.a: The match was cancelled because of the storm.
items.b: The match was cancelled ___ the storm.
items.tip: because of = due to.
items.say: The match was cancelled due to the storm.

items.a: Lucy probably won't come to the party.
items.tip: probably won't = is unlikely to + verb.
items.say: Lucy is unlikely to come to the party.

items.a: Can you look after my hamster this weekend?
items.b: Can you ___ my hamster this weekend?
items.tip: look after = take care of.
items.say: Can you take care of my hamster this weekend?

items.a: I didn't expect the test to be so easy.
items.tip: didn't expect it to be so easy = it was easier than I expected.
items.say: The test was much easier than I expected.
